title: The first power saving over n^{4/3} for planar unit distances since 1984: OpenAI's 53-page proof holds as read by nine hostile seats, and the Euclidean step Valtr's metric cannot take is the reciprocal jump w − w′ = 1/(z − z′)
line: Erdős's unit distance conjecture is false (OpenAI, May 2026: n^{1+c}); the upper bound has been Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter's n^{4/3} for 42 years, and the page says why — a different metric attains it. OpenAI's 23 September paper complexifies the unit circle into zw = 1 and proves no configuration can have t^{4−o(1)} unit pairs: bounded jump heights die on a 3-neighbour determinant, unbounded ones on an entropy-prediction device, a product-formula score budget and a Kummer-theory obstruction in an ultraproduct. Nine seats verified every lemma line by line with instruments that fail on controls; the Euclidean input sits in exactly four places; two exposition defects found. A 40-file Lean proof is in the release but not in its catalogue — our kernel replay is queued and this card is updated when it reports.
